title: Prado reunites Valeriano Bécquer's complete series on Spanish popular life for the first time
summary: The Museo Nacional del Prado has reunited, for the first time, a remarkable group of eight paintings in which Valeriano Domínguez Bécquer captured the clothing, celebrations, labor and religious traditions of 19th-century Spain. Presented under the title Valeriano D. Bécquer (1834–1870): Paintings of Popular Customs, the exhibition brings together works commissioned for the former Museo de la Trinidad and later dispersed among different institutions. The series is now on view in Gallery 60 as part of the Prado’s “Open Storage” program, an initiative devoted to revealing new perspectives on the museum’s 19th-century collections. Bécquer completed the paintings between 1866 and 1867, traveling through Zaragoza, Soria and Ávila in search of scenes that reflected the everyday customs of rural Spain. title: Inside Job: Christie's New York staff art show
summary: Christie's announced its annual summer Staff Art Auction: Inside Job. The online sale is open for bidding from August 5 to August 19 and features a curated selection of artworks created by Christie's talented staff from the New York City headquarters. The sale showcases a diverse group of art and design across categories created by Christie's colleagues from various departments including: client service representatives, art handlers, specialists, photographers, administrators and product developers. With estimates starting at $100, the auction is an opportunity for seasoned collectors and those just embarking on their collecting journey. Works from the sale will be on view at Christie's Rockefeller Center galleries from August 14 to August 18. The buyer's premium from this sale will be donated to Publicolor, a nonprofit that harnesses the transformative power of art

title: Decorative Art Deco and Mid-Century items top Roland's July 25th Summer Auction
summary: Roland Auctions NY presented over 800 lots at their July 25th, 2026 Multi-Estates Auction, their first sale of the summer season. A unique collection of Art Deco furnishings and Decorative items from a private New York City collector were some of the top sellers of the day, while Fine and Contemporary Art once again took the main stage with a strong presence at Roland. The group of Art Deco/Mid-Century decorative items, all from a private Manhattan collection got much of the attention, with the actual top seller of the day being an exquisite Art Deco RCA Victor Television console, 1st half 20th century, waterfall design in mahogany and ribbed dark wood trim, that sold for $18,200, a very unique Sparton Model 5470 Tube Radio Art Deco chrome table-top radio, circa 1940's, with red Bakelite mounts and clear push button knobs, went for $845 and an After Paul T. title: Grant Zahajko Auctions announces move to Nevada following final Davenport sale
summary: Grant Zahajko Auctions will bid a fond farewell to its longtime home in Davenport with a Sports Cards & Memorabilia, Comic Books, Autographs + Collectibles auction on Wednesday, August 12th, online and live at the gallery. After that the company will relocate to Mesquite, Nevada this fall. Grant Zahjkjo Auctions has enjoyed a fine working relationship with the city of Davenport and the auction-going citizenry since its founding in 2016. The firm was attracted to the city’s small-town lifestyle, friendly people, affordability as a startup and its proximity to the international airport, since owners Grant and Gina Zahajko often travel the country, picking up consignments. title: Kirchner Museum Davos explores artist's use of color in new exhibition
summary: With luminous contrasts, vibrating fields of colour and radical expressive power, Ernst Ludwig Kirchner created a visual language that continues to captivate audiences and scientists alike. This summer, the Kirchner Museum Davos dedicates an extraordinary exhibition to the medium of colour: “A Rush of Colour” traces the journey of colour from Kirchner’s canvas to the laboratory – from pigment to its impact on the retina. No sooner has one colour spectacle faded than the next arrives in Davos. Following the historic public success of “Kirchner. Picasso”, the Kirchner Museum Davos now turns its attention to what makes Kirchner’s work truly distinctive: colour. From summer onwards, this exploration of colour also takes to the streets, appearing as a sea of flags along Davos’s Promenade and Talstrasse – the very landscapes that inspired Kirchner’s unique world of colour. title: Pacific Cultures Gallery to undergo delicate conservation program
summary: The South Australian Museum is commencing a major conservation and cultural care program for its Pacific Cultures collection, ensuring significant pieces are preserved for future generations. Many important cultural items in the Pacific Cultures Gallery have been on display for decades and require essential specialist conservation for their long-term preservation. Work is being delivered in partnership with the Pacific Islands Council of South Australia (PICSA) and Pasifika community leaders, ensuring cultural knowledge, authority and protocols guide the care and stewardship of ancestral objects. Museum visitors are encouraged to come in before the end of the month to see this important conservation project as it begins. Conservation work in the Pacific Cultures Gallery will begin shortly, with the gallery scheduled to close to the public from Monday 3 August. title: See London's only Blue Period Picasso in a trip around turn-of-the-century Europe at the National Gallery
summary: Visitors can experience the art scenes of Barcelona, Berlin and Paris at the beginning of the 20th century through three new loans coming to the National Gallery from the start of August. In Room 45, our collection of works by Paul Cezanne, Edgar Degas and George Bellows will be enriched by two exceptional loans: a stunning painting by the American artist Marsden Hartley (1877–1943), and the only Blue Period work by Pablo Picasso (1881–1973) currently on display in a London museum. In Room 46 our collection of Claude Monet’s (1840–1927) paintings will be expanded with Waterlilies (1905). In 1913 American-born Hartley moved to Berlin, known for its experimental art scene. During his years in the city he painted his Amerika series, of which Painting No. 50 (1914–15) is a part. title: Exhibition at Ludwig Múzeum highlights neo-avant-garde legacy
summary: The exhibition presents the ART FOND Collection from Bratislava, in which the neo-avant-garde strategies of late modernism remain urgently relevant today. Rather than a closed historical phenomenon, the neo-avant-garde appears here as a lasting mode of resistance, critical thinking, and civic responsibility, continuously reactivated in contemporary artistic practice. The exhibition title, borrowed from a work by Kristián Németh, functions as a political and ethical proposition. It asserts that art grounded in freedom, critical awareness, and the courage to question power structures cannot reach an endpoint. In times marked by renewed ideological pressure, cultural censorship, and the erosion of institutional autonomy, the idea of “no end” becomes a statement against closure, silencing, and historical amnesia. title: National Academy of Design revives Artist's Eye Series with Shelter from the Storm
summary: The National Academy of Design presents Shelter from the Storm: An Artist's Eye with Stan Allen and Polly Apfelbaum, an exhibition on view September 17, 2026 through January 16, 2027, at the National Academy's gallery, 519 West 26th Street, 2nd Floor, New York City. Marking the return of The Artist's Eye exhibition series for the first time since 2013, the exhibition brings together eighty works from the Academy's collection to examine how artists and architects have responded to periods of upheaval, uncertainty, and transformation throughout American history. Co-curated by architect Stan Allen and artist Polly Apfelbaum, Shelter from the Storm serves as the culminating exhibition of the National Academy's bicentennial anniversary year and is the largest collection-based exhibition to be presented

title: Foam unveils 15 emerging photography artists selected for Foam Talent 2026
summary: Foam presents Foam Talent 2026. A group exhibition showcasing work of an extraordinary new wave of image-makers shaping the future of photography. This year’s exhibition features the work of 15 extraordinary artists, chosen from nearly 2,892 submissions from 107 countries. The 15 Foam Talents in the exhibition reflect the energy, diversity, and global reach of emerging photographic practices today. Together, their practices point towards bold new directions in the medium and present a strong commitment to storytelling across a range of narratives, perspectives, and artistic approaches. At a time marked by constant global change and uncertainty, the Foam Talent’s engage with some of the most pressing themes in photography and society today: political oppression, grief, and mental health, religion and faith, conflict, displacement, cultural identity, and technological innovation. title: Carpenters Workshop Gallery presents dual exhibition by Martin Lafort and Léa Mestres
summary: In a new exhibition titled Small Car, Big Windows, French artists and designers Martin Laforêt and Léa Mestres reflect on how perspectives and observations are shaped by journeys and movements through shifting landscapes. While both maintain separate, individual practices, this exhibition at Carpenters Workshop Gallery in London brings them into a shared, collaborative dialogue, with new works of sculptural design – including tables, seating and lighting pieces – that provide a personal look into the designers’ current way of life and how it shapes their creativity. Often moving between living in Paris and working in Brittany, Laforêt and Mestres observe the changing landscape of northern France, from the harsh concrete of the built urban environment to the natural shapes and colours of the countryside. title: Moderna Museet presents post-war Swedish art in new collection exhibition
summary: Moderna Museet’s new exhibition of works from the collection borrows its title from Peter Tillberg’s well-known painting “Will You Be Profitable, Little Friend?” (1972). The exhibition features around a hundred artworks from the period 1945–1979, many of which have had a central place in the museum’s exhibition history since its opening in 1958. For many visitors, it means an opportunity to revisit familiar artworks, while younger ones get the chance to discover them for the first time. The Moderna Museet collection contains a strong representation of Swedish art from the post-war period. The exhibition “Will You Be Profitable, Little Friend?” highlights the diversity of artistic expressions and moods that characterised the era, when Swedish society and the surrounding world were changing at a rapid pace. title: Prado journeys into the ancient world with art inspired by Homer's Odyssey
summary: As Christopher Nolan brings Homer’s Odyssey to the screen, the Museo Nacional del Prado is inviting audiences to explore how artists have imagined the ancient world across more than two millennia. The Madrid museum has released a new video that brings together 24 paintings, sculptures and drawings inspired by classical mythology, the Trojan War and the perilous journeys at the heart of Greek and Roman storytelling. Set to Dinamita, a song by Spanish musician La Bien Querida, the sequence moves from the Judgment of Paris and the abduction of Helen to the burning of Troy, the travels of Aeneas and the ordeals of Odysseus. Rather than offering a conventional art-historical lecture, the project creates an emotional and cinematic journey through the Prado’s collection. title: MUDEC presents immersive white thread installation by Chiharu Shiota
summary: The Moment the Snow Melts is a new immersive, site-specific installation by Japanese artist Chiharu Shiota, which reimagines the Agora—the heart of MUDEC. The installation transforms this iconic space into an evanescent landscape of white threads cascading vertically from the ceiling. Suspended among them are notes and pieces of paper inscribed with the names of individuals who have crossed our paths, but with whom connections have since been severed. Even before the opening, the public was invited to participate in the installation by contributing personal thoughts or drawings on paper—submitted via a dedicated collection box within the museum or submitted digitally. title: Five new Trustees appointed to the Board of the Science Museum Group
summary: Priya Guha, Professor Thomas Solomon and Toufic Machnouk are among five new Science Museum Group Trustees announced by the Prime Minister. Priya Guha MBE is a member of the UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) Board and a Venture Partner at Merian Ventures. Toufic Machnouk is Managing Director of GBRX, the strategic innovation body for Britain's railway, and a member of the National Railway Museum Advisory Board. Professor Thomas Solomon CBE is Director of the Pandemic Institute and of the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Health Protection Research Unit in Emerging and Zoonotic Infections in Liverpool. title: Ashmolean Museum announces major autumn exhibition exploring the image of Aphrodite
summary: The civilisations that first created Aphrodite disappeared long ago. Her image never did. There are few figures in human history, fewer women still, whose fame has lasted for 5,000 years. Aphrodite’s story stretches from ancient Cyprus to the present day. Immortalised by Botticelli, who gave her one of the most recognisable faces in the history of art, and endlessly reinterpreted through the ages, Aphrodite and her Roman counterpart, Venus, remain defining symbols of beauty and desire in Western culture. The Ashmolean’s autumn exhibition explores one of the ancient world’s most enduring cultural icons. Bringing together archaeology, sculpture, painting, contemporary art and fashion, The Making of a Goddess traces Aphrodite’s journey and transformations from her earliest origins in the eastern Mediterranean, through the ancient Greek and Roman worlds,

title: European Prize for Urban Public Space selects 25 projects addressing climate, mobility and social inclusion
summary: Twenty-five projects from across Europe have been shortlisted for the 2026 European Prize for Urban Public Space, reflecting a growing effort to rethink how cities respond to climate change, social inequality and the changing demands of mobility. Organized by the Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona, the prize received a record 381 submissions from 38 European countries this year. The selected projects come from 14 countries and include interventions in major cities such as Paris, Copenhagen, Barcelona, Lisbon, Brussels, Vienna and Warsaw. Rather than favoring a single type of architectural gesture, the shortlist brings together projects of widely different scales and ambitions. title: Prado publishes Roberto Longhi's lost essay linking Pedro Berruguete to the court of Urbino
summary: More than a century after it was written, a lost essay by the influential Italian art historian Roberto Longhi is being published for the first time by the Museo Nacional del Prado. The text, devoted to the Castilian painter Pedro Berruguete, appears in El solemnísimo maestro Pedro Berruguete, the fifth volume in the Prado’s Bicentennial Collection. Edited by art historian Tommaso Mozzati, the book brings into print a study that helped launch a major and still unresolved debate about artistic exchange between Spain and Italy during the Renaissance. Longhi conceived the essay after traveling through Spain in the summer of 1920. During a visit to the Prado, he began to consider the possibility that Berruguete, one of the leading painters active in late 15th-century Castile, had spent an extended period at the court of Federico da Montefeltro in Urbino. title: NADA announces exhibitor list for NADA Miami 2026
summary: NADA announces over 130 participating galleries and artists for the 24th edition of NADA Miami, to take place December 1–5, 2026 at Ice Palace Studios. The NADA Miami art fair brings together exhibitors from 63 cities and 27 countries, including Lagos, Havana, Tokyo, Buenos Aires, and Kansas City. This year’s fair welcomes 45 first-time exhibitors, including Pietro Alexander (New York), Clauda (Prague), Forgotten Lands (Christiansted), Real Tinsel (Milwaukee), and Slip House (New York), and features 59 NADA Gallery Members, including Burnaway (Atlanta), Entrance (New York), Gattopardo (Los Angeles), Misako & Rosen (Tokyo), Pangée (Montreal), Piedras (Buenos Aires), Proxyco Gallery (New York), and Andrew Rafacz (Chicago). Participants are selected through a competitive application and peer review process. NADA

title: First US solo show for Japanese artist Katsumi Nakai on view at Polina Berlin Gallery
summary: Polina Berlin Gallery is presenting Katsumi Nakai: Works 1965-1997, a collection of works by the late Japanese artist Katsumi Nakai (1927-2013) that span a three-decade period of the artist’s defining years in Milan. This presentation marks the first solo gallery exhibition in the United States for the artist, as well as marking the 70-year anniversary of the artist’s first ever solo exhibition held in Osaka in 1956. Katsumi Nakai was born in 1927 in Hirakata, Osaka, and in 1953, he entered the Institute of Fine Arts of Osaka to study painting. Nakai belonged to a generation of artists who spent their formative years of working in Japan during the aftermath of the Second World War. title: Museum of the City of New York displays restored WPA Alice in Wonderland murals
summary: The Museum of the City of New York is presenting Another Wonderland: Abram Champanier’s Alice Mural, an exhibition spotlighting the rescue and restoration of New York’s most whimsical and historically significant public mural series. Another Wonderland brings to light a remarkable example of New Deal-era public art, Alice of Wonderland Visiting New York, a mural cycle created by Abram Champanier for the children’s ward at Gouverneur Hospital between 1938 and 1940. Commissioned through the Works Progress Administration’s (WPA) Federal Art Project, Champanier reimagined Lewis Carroll’s Alice in Wonderland in 1930s New York City. The result was a sixteen-panel mural—each panel over seven feet tall—blending fantasy and city life to uplift young patients and hospital staff, and adding color, movement, and magic

title: Museums partner to present 'Louisiana Couture: The Legacy of San Carlin'
summary: The Louisiana Art & Science Museum (LASM) and the LSU Textile & Costume Museum (LSUTCM) are presenting Louisiana Couture: The Legacy of San Carlin, a landmark exhibition celebrating one of Louisiana's most influential fashion houses. Currently on view at LASM, the exhibition showcases the artistry, craftsmanship, and entrepreneurial spirit behind San Carlin, the Baton Rouge couture label whose elegant designs earned international acclaim while remaining proudly rooted in Louisiana. Drawn from the LSU Textile & Costume Museum's extensive San Carlin archive, the exhibition represents a significant collaboration between LSUTCM and LASM to share this remarkable chapter of Louisiana's cultural history with a broader audience. title: Bodleian Libraries host major exhibition on humanity's relationship with birds
summary: The Bodleian Libraries announced their exhibition, Wonder of Birds, which explores humanity’s enduring relationship with birds through the dual lens of awe and loss. The exhibition is inspired by The Book of Birds produced by award-winning collaborators artist Jackie Morris and writer Robert Macfarlane. Both book and exhibition lament the decline of our avian companions at the same time as celebrating their unique characteristics and cultural significance. With original artwork and prose from their book, shown in conversation with the Bodleian’s astonishing collections, the exhibition is presented through ‘Seven Wonders’ from nest, egg, beak and song, to feather, flight and migration.
